behavioral_effects: A view-only share recipient can no longer rename, archive, or delete a shared conversation; an edit-share recipient can rename and archive but not delete; hard delete is owner-only.
The open finding view-share-can-modify-conversations in the 2026-08-20 fix-critical-security-findings change record is closed and Summary.md regenerated, open findings 7 to 6.
compatibility_impact: No request or response shape changes and no proxy handler changes. PATCH /api/v1/conversations/{id} and POST /{id}/archive now return 403 for view-only share recipients; DELETE /{id} returns 403 for any non-owner share recipient. Owner behavior, edit-share rename and archive, and admin surfaces are unchanged. The WS agent auto-title path now rejects a view-only recipient at the title update instead of one call later at add_message - the same AuthorizationError outcome.

reason: ConversationService.get_conversation granted non-owner access whenever any share row existed, ignoring share.permission, so a view-only share recipient could rename, archive, or hard-delete the owner's conversation via PATCH, POST-archive, and DELETE /api/v1/conversations/{id}; update and archive now require an edit share and delete requires ownership, closing open finding view-share-can-modify-conversations
risks: user_id=None remains the trusted unscoped path for admin routes and internal callers; a future caller that omits the actor silently bypasses every share check. Unchanged from the prior session, mitigated by the regression tests and docstrings on all three write paths.
rollback: git revert of the single commit restores the vulnerable write paths, restores the deleted check_edit_permission, and reopens the finding in the prior change record; run make governance-sync afterwards to regenerate Summary.md. No schema or data migration involved.
security_impact: Closes the high-severity view-share-can-modify-conversations finding. update_conversation and archive_conversation now authorize through get_conversation with require_edit=True, so a view-only share recipient receives 403 instead of renaming or archiving the shared conversation; delete_conversation passes the new require_owner flag, so hard delete is owner-only and every share tier receives 403. Users with no share still receive 404 so conversation existence is not disclosed. Admin routes and internal callers keep the deliberate user_id=None trusted path. The orphaned ConversationShareService.check_edit_permission was deleted, leaving get_conversation as the single conversation authorization primitive.
summary: Require edit shares for conversation update/archive and restrict delete to owners
